newsitem.title: JAPAN: MITI panel urges reform of Japan's withholding tax.
newsitem.headline: MITI panel urges reform of Japan's withholding tax.

text.p: Exempting foreign investors from Japan's withholding tax on interest income would substantially reduce the cost to the Japanese government of issuing bonds, an advisory panel to the Trade Ministry said on Wednesday.
Foreign investors are currently subject to a 20 percent withholding tax on interest earned from Japanese bonds.

The tax was making Japanese bonds less attractive to foreign investors, the subcommittee for industrial finance, which advises the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI), said in a statement.

The subcommittee said bonds issued in the euro primary bond market by Japanese public financial institutions trade at yields roughly the same as or even lower than Japanese government bonds (JGBs), although government-guaranteed bonds, by contrast, consistently trade at a yield five to 20 basis points higher than the equivalent JGB.
This difference reflects the fact that bonds issued in the euro market are exempt from the withholding tax, the subcommittee said.
It added that the withholding tax adds an estimated 10 basis points to yields of JGBs and Japanese corporate bonds.
The subcommittee said exempting foreign investors from the withholding tax would in the initial year result in a loss of some 6.1 billion yen in tax revenue.
In the future, however, the exemption could help the government save about 233 billion yen in annual interest payments, the subcommittee said.
The subcommittee, made up of 19 members including academics, company directors and economists, plans to finalise its financial reform proposals by early June.
